record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can dynamic scheduling be implemented in user-centric cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) when the total user population greatly exceeds the number of users that can be active on each time-frequency resource block, coding and decoding occur block by block rather than over infinitely many fading states, scheduled rates must account for outage probability, pilot-contamination conflicts constrain simultaneous users, and long-term throughput should remain fair?

evidence.quote: I. How to Implement Dynamic Scheduling?
This assumption may be incompatible with dynamic scheduling and per-slot coding/decoding, as well as with low-latency requirements, which are key features of 5G [144], [145].

The scheduler must allocate an “instantaneous” rate to each active user since encoding/decoding is performed block by block, i.e., coding over a virtually infinite sequence of fading states is not possible.

The problem of dynamic scheduling in user-centric CF-MMIMO networks where the number of total users is much larger than the number of simultaneously active users on each time-frequency RB has not been widely investigated and remains quite open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a user-centric cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) wireless network with $L$ geographically distributed remote radio units (RRUs), each equipped with $M$ antennas, jointly serving a total population of $K_{\mathrm{tot}}$ single-antenna user equipments (UEs). Communication occurs over time-frequency resource blocks (RBs). On each RB, only a subset $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\{1,\dots,K_{\mathrm{tot}}\}$ of users with $|\mathcal{A}|\ll K_{\mathrm{tot}}$ can be simultaneously active because: (i) uplink pilot resources are limited to $\tau_p$ orthogonal sequences, so pilot reuse among co-scheduled users induces pilot contamination, modeled by a conflict graph $G=(V,E)$ where $V=\{1,\dots,K_{\mathrm{tot}}\}$ and an edge $\{i,j\}\in E$ forbids $i$ and $j$ from being simultaneously scheduled; (ii) each user $k$ is associated with a cluster $\mathcal{C}_k\subseteq\{1,\dots,L\}$ of serving RRUs.

Encoding and decoding are performed block by block on each RB (no coding across infinitely many fading states), so for each scheduled user $k$ at time $t$ the achievable rate must be associated with a target outage probability $\epsilon\in(0,1)$: the scheduler assigns an instantaneous rate $R_k(t)$ such that $\Pr\!\left(\log_2(1+\mathrm{SINR}_k(t)) < R_k(t)\right)\le \epsilon$, where $\mathrm{SINR}_k(t)$ depends on the active set $\mathcal{A}(t)$, the precoder/combiner used, the channel estimates and the residual pilot contamination.

Let $\bar R_k(T):=\tfrac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbf{1}\{k\in\mathcal{A}(t)\}\,R_k(t)$ denote the long-term average throughput of user $k$.

Problem. Design and analyze a dynamic scheduling policy that, at each RB $t$, selects an active subset $\mathcal{A}(t)$ that is an independent set of the conflict graph $G$ and an instantaneous rate vector $\{R_k(t)\}_{k\in\mathcal{A}(t)}$ with per-user outage at most $\epsilon$, so as to maximize a fairness criterion on the long-term throughputs, e.g.
$$\max\ \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{tot}}} \log \bar R_k(\infty) \qquad\text{(proportional fairness),}$$
or equivalently to maximize $\min_k \bar R_k(\infty)$ (max-min fairness), under the constraints that $K_{\mathrm{tot}}\gg |\mathcal{A}(t)|$, that only causal channel-state information is available, and that the policy is implementable with bounded per-slot complexity. Establish optimality guarantees (e.g., convergence to the optimum of the corresponding network utility maximization), characterize the resulting feasible long-term rate region under outage constraints and pilot-contamination conflicts, and quantify performance loss relative to the ergodic (infinite-blocklength) benchmark.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 work ("Fairness Scheduling in User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO Wireless Networks", arXiv:2307.00850) proposes a conflict-graph based dynamic scheduling policy that forbids simultaneous scheduling of users with large pilot contamination and uses per-slot service rates modeled via information outage probability, addressing the same setting. This and related works (e.g., "Improving Fairness for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Through Interference-Aware Massive Access") provide partial solutions and heuristics, but a fully general optimal scheduling framework with provable guarantees for the regime $K_{\mathrm{tot}}\gg|\mathcal{A}(t)|$ under outage and pilot-contamination constraints remains an active research area.

status_evidence.title: Fairness Scheduling in User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO Wireless Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Conflict graph prevents simultaneous scheduling of users with large pilot contamination; per-slot service rates modeled using information outage probability; adaptive instantaneous service-rate scheduling robust to system uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a partial solution: a fairness scheduling algorithm in user-centric CF-MMIMO using a pilot-contamination conflict graph and outage-based instantaneous rates.

status_evidence.title: Improving Fairness for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Through Interference-Aware Massive Access
status_evidence.snippet: Interference-aware massive access scheme improving fairness in cell-free massive MIMO.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial solution addressing fairness and interference (including pilot contamination) in CF-MMIMO access scheduling.

status_evidence.title: Fairness Scheduling in Dense User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks
status_evidence.claim: Further work studying scheduling and fairness in dense user-centric CF-MMIMO.
